hints.title: Constant Time Board Victory Detection
hints.text: Checking an entire row, column, and diagonal on every move takes linear time. How can numeric counters track progress toward victory in constant time?

hints.title: Signed Row, Column, and Diagonal Counters
hints.text: Assign player one a value of +1 and player two a value of -1. Maintain arrays for rows and columns, and two scalars for the main and anti-diagonals.

hints.title: O(1) Move Evaluation Blueprint
hints.text: Add points (+1 or -1) to rows[row] and cols[col]. If row == col, add points to diagonal. If row + col == n - 1, add points to anti-diagonal. If the absolute value of any updated counter equals n, current player wins.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Updates at most 4 counters per move in constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all rows, columns, and diagonals per move takes O(N) time, leading to O(N^3) total game simulation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Linear O(N) memory stores running sums for each line, enabling O(1) decision per move.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly identifying both main diagonal (row == col) and anti-diagonal (row + col == n - 1).
